modules.name: Start with a baseline
modules.what: Name the AI uses you want and the data each needs. Score your organisation on five dimensions, with evidence for each score.
modules.make: A baseline scorecard and three use cases

modules.name: Know your data
modules.what: List every data source with an owner and a sensitivity level. Write quality checks and a data contract for one dataset.
modules.tools: DataHub, OpenMetadata, Pandera, Great Expectations Core
modules.make: A data inventory and one data contract

modules.name: Make it searchable
modules.what: Turn PDFs and scans into clean text. Search by meaning, then test it on questions your staff really ask, with access rules on.
modules.make: A working search over your own documents, and its test results

modules.name: Platform, law and cost
modules.what: Design the path from source to search with a check at each step. Map your data to four national laws. Price a hosting option.
modules.make: A reference architecture, a data protection map and a cost estimate

modules.name: Govern and plan
modules.what: Set roles, a policy and a risk register using NIST and ISO 42001. Sequence a twelve-month plan and present it as a board paper.
modules.make: A twelve-month roadmap and a board presentation

sessions.title: What AI-ready data means
sessions.q: Which AI uses do we want, and what data does each one need?
sessions.demo: Ask a language model the same question over a folder with and without the current policy file, and see the stale answer.
sessions.make: Three use cases with their data needs

sessions.title: Score your readiness
sessions.demo: Score the case organisation on five dimensions and five levels, then defend each score with evidence.

sessions.title: Find, own and catalogue your data
sessions.q: Who owns each source, and who may see it?
sessions.demo: Scan a database and a shared folder into a data catalogue and read the lineage.
sessions.make: Inventory of ten sources with owner and sensitivity

sessions.title: Quality, metadata and data contracts
sessions.q: How do we know a dataset is fit for AI use?
sessions.demo: Write checks against a customer table with seeded defects, then write the contract.
sessions.make: Quality rules and a contract for one dataset

sessions.title: From documents to clean text
sessions.q: Which of our documents can AI read, and what must be repaired first?
sessions.demo: Parse PDFs, scans and spreadsheets, split them into chunks and attach metadata.

sessions.title: Search by meaning
sessions.q: What does search by meaning add to the keyword search we have?
sessions.demo: Embed the chunks, store them in a vector index and combine keyword and meaning search.
sessions.make: A working search over the sample documents

sessions.title: Test the search and control who sees what
sessions.q: Can we trust the results, and does the search respect permissions?
sessions.demo: Write 30 test questions, measure how often the right passage is found, then add permission filters.

sessions.title: Pipelines and platform design
sessions.q: How does data travel from source to search, and who is told when it breaks?
sessions.demo: Schedule ingest, check and embed steps, store files as Parquet and trace one record end to end.

sessions.title: Privacy and East African law
sessions.q: What does the law require when AI reads personal data?
sessions.demo: Find and mask personal data in documents, then map the findings to four national laws.
sessions.make: A data protection map for the organisation

sessions.title: Hosting, cost and licences
sessions.q: Where should this run, and what will it cost?
sessions.demo: Compare on-site, local data centre, South African cloud region and a local open model, and read the licence files.
sessions.make: A costed hosting option and a licence register

sessions.title: Governance and AI risk
sessions.q: Who decides, who answers for it, and what happens when it goes wrong?
sessions.demo: Walk an incident through the four NIST functions and fill in a risk register.
sessions.make: Roles, a policy and a risk register

sessions.title: Your twelve-month roadmap
sessions.q: What do we do first, and what do we ask the board for?
sessions.demo: Sequence the work against the baseline, price it and present it.
